coverageAndMeaningReview.notes: Original heading identity and page identity remain unchanged; the English modern title conveys diffraction gratings. No dates or named historical entities occur in this lesson.

Diffraction, narrow parallel slits, opaque intervals, glass ruling, several thousand lines per 1 millimeter, total exceeding 100000, gelatin impressions, and reflecting/scattering strips are otherwise covered. The original quality ranking is attributed rather than newly verified. Fig-206 is a magnifier, not another slit array.
Both figure IDs and caption numbers are retained. English visible captions do not change source identities. No figure approval follows from this reference check.

a and b are slit/interval widths, or reflecting/scattering-strip widths; d=a+b is the repeat distance between corresponding positions, not b alone. Wavelength, monochromatic illumination and parallel illumination are defined. Normal incidence and uniform spacing explicitly scope the derivation and agree with fig-207.

Secondary waves are a propagation model, not new lamps. Phi is measured from the grating normal. A and B are corresponding adjacent-slit edges, C is on the outgoing ray from A, and BC is perpendicular to that ray. The comparison wavefront gives AC as extra path; integer wavelengths imply matching phase for the common incident wave. The repaired final AC restores the source literal without a new geometric claim.

The complete formula |AC|=|AB| sin(phi)=d sin(phi) remains literal. AB is the hypotenuse and repeat distance; AC is its projection onto the outgoing direction. In the right triangle the angle equal to the viewing phi is at B, so AC is the opposite leg. Both explanations are consistent; no extra numeric geometry or small-angle replacement is supplied.

Equation d sin(phi)=k lambda, label 7.9 and the original nonnegative integer list remain unchanged. Zero and successive orders are explained, matching directions on the other side are scoped to the same normal incidence, and the sine bound distinguishes allowed directions from an unlimited order list.

Corresponding points in neighboring slits are separated by d and have the same k lambda path difference. This does not assert that all positions within one slit reinforce each other. The explicit single-slit qualifier correctly allows unequal strengths and canceled orders without changing the original maxima equation or inventing a calibrated envelope.

Converging lens follows the grating; screen is in its focal plane. Same-direction rays are focused together in the source's schematic model. Screen displacement is not grating spacing, and a quantitative length requires focal length. No exact universal ray law, aberration-free physical apparatus, screen-distance calibration or invented focal-length value is claimed.

Different wavelengths separate in nonzero allowed orders; zero order overlaps them centrally. Farther displacement for longer wavelength explicitly fixes grating and order. Possible inter-order overlap does not change wavelength. Citation suffixes IV,1 and printed irregular IV2,3 remain literal; no IV,2,3 erratum is inferred and no plate contents or modern plate availability are approved.

Known spacing and measured angle determine wavelength only after identifying a nonzero order and respecting the derivation's incidence conditions. Zero order cannot distinguish wavelengths this way. No example values, new equation or precision calibration are invented.

Eyelash gaps, rainbow observation, well-used record grooves, reflected lamp light, multiple k spectra and relatively large incidence angle are retained as source descriptions. Neither locale instructs staring into intense light. The record is explicitly an oblique-incidence observation, not an unqualified application of the normal-incidence equation; the grooves do not create new colored light.
Both exercise arrays remain empty and retain the zero-task raw source. No original or invented task is added.

diagramObservationsForTextOnly.observation: Parallel vertical ruling on a rectangular surface; circular magnifier and handle show enlarged ruling. No printed exact slit count, numeric scale or a/b/d dimensions. Text supplies transmission properties, not an inferred dark/light assignment.

Horizontal incident arrows meet a vertical grating normally. A and B lie at corresponding lower edges of adjacent slits, with vertical d marking their separation. Outgoing rays are parallel and rise rightwards. C lies on A's ray; dashed BC is perpendicular to that ray. Phi is drawn between the grating normal and outgoing direction. Rays bend at the converging-lens symbol toward one screen point. No numeric angle, wavelength, focal length, spacing or calibrated brightness is printed.
